chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Kalbi from Amr ibn Khald from Zayd ibn Ali from his fathers from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

A man from the family of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sought permission [to enter] and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said to him: 'I advise you not to associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut into pieces and burnt with fire; and do not disobey your parents, and if they wish you to leave your world, then leave it; and do not curse people; and when you meet your Muslim brother, greet him with a cheerful face and pour for him the extra water from your bucket. Convey to the Muslims you meet salutations from me, and invite people to Islam, and be sure that for each person who responds to you, you will gain the reward of freeing a slave from the descendants of Jacob, and teach them that al-Sughra is forbidden upon them, meaning Nabidh, which is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings and social etiquettes advised by the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the lineage of Zayd ibn Ali, encapsulates a comprehensive ethical code linking theological fidelity (Tawhid) with social conduct, emphasizing that steadfastness in monotheism justifies enduring hardship. It highlights the Shia emphasis on parental obedience as a primary duty and the prophetic etiquette of cheerful greeting (Bashshar) and resource sharing (Sadaqah) to foster communal unity. The clarification of Nabidh as Khamr underscores the principle that any intoxicant is prohibited, a ruling derived from the broader Quranic prohibition of intoxicants.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 22.Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Kalbī narrated from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his fathers, from ʿAlī (a) who said,

“A man sought permission from the family of the Messenger of Allah (ṣ) to enter [his house], then he said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, advise me.’ He (ṣ) said to him, ‘I advise you not to ascribe any partners to Allah – even if you are cut into pieces and burnt with fire, and not to disobey your parents – if they wish you to leave your [position in this] world then leave it, and not to curse people, and when you meet your Muslim brother, meet him with a cheerful face, and pour for him the extra water you have in your bucket.[1] Convey to the Muslims you meet salutations from me, and invite people to Islam – be sure that [in doing so,] for each person who responds [positively] to you, you will gain the reward of freeing a slave from the descendants of [Prophet] Yaʿqūb, and teach them that alṣughrāb [or al-ṣughayrāʾ] is forbidden upon them, meaning nabīdh, which is a [kind of] wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden.’”
